speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: asked the Minister for Manpower in view of the recent spate of workplace fatal accidents (a) whether there are common causes of the accidents; (b) which are the sectors where such accidents are more prevalent; (c) whether the current framework of measures is adequate; and (d) what new measures may be needed to prevent industrial accidents in future.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: To address this, the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) works with companies to raise awareness of accident risks in their workplaces.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Besides engaging industry associations like the Singapore Contractors Association Limited and the Commercial Diving Association of Singapore, we also issue regular alerts to share learning points from recent accidents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: For example, we have notified companies on the dangers of improper use of material hoists, which led to a fatal accident in a food factory.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: We issued reminders on the proper procedures for doing construction work, especially at heights, as falls have accounted for about half of construction fatalities this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: We will continue to adopt a mix of targeted enforcement while raising awareness on safety lapses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: To achieve sustained improvements in workplace safety and health (WSH), we convened the WSH2028 Tripartite Strategy Committee to recommend new approaches.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: It will share its preliminary recommendations at the Singapore WSH Conference later this month.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I take it that the Minister of State is taking Question No 29 as well?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: But I note that the number of fatalities has been higher in the first part of 2018 compared to that the year before.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Certainly, this year, we saw an increase and largely driven by the construction sector.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In May, I announced that we are conducting additional inspections, about 500 inspections, and we also extended another 250 when we saw fatalities in the construction sector still increasing.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We have completed about 80% of the extended inspections.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: What we have done so far is to issue six stop-work orders and 164 composition fines amounting to $188,750.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We hope that this will send a strong message to the construction sector to be more vigilant, especially since they have contributed a significant amount of fatalities to the workplaces this year.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But it is not just the construction sector that we are working on.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We have also been working with the manufacturing and commercial diving sector as well, which have also contributed some amount of fatalities this year.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, it is an area that we are constantly working on, but we hope that employers make conscious decisions to mitigate risks at the worksites to reduce fatalities.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I note that there are higher incidences of foreign workers in construction worksites falling victim to workplace accidents.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I think the Minister of State's reply says that the fatality rate is higher for the foreign workers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Are there any plans by MOM to focus on education and raising awareness among this group of foreign workers?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: MOM and WSH Council both reach out to workers through various means, such as roadshows, events at dormitories and on weekends, to convey these messages to foreign workers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I think it is also important that as they settle in, especially for those working in construction, to be trained in terms of safety aspects since they come from different backgrounds.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We also ensure that WSH collaterals are printed in different languages so that workers from different nationalities are also able to benefit from the different advice.
